why: Conditional engineering sensitivity experiment, NOT a calibrated town exposure model. world=scene holds the displayed traffic fixed. exposure=1 means one injected bicycle card per designed episode by construction, NOT one encounter per real-world trip; do not use it to compare per-trip risk to bus_bypass. x=10..40 m brackets the chosen x=25 m on the simulated straight street, away from the marked crosswalk at x=122 m. Bicycle speed 3.5..4.5 m/s (12.6..16.2 km/h) is a deliberately narrow low-speed sensitivity range within the 12..20 km/h observations discussed in FHWA-HRT-05-137 chapter 2 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/publications/research/safety/pedbike/05137/chapter2.cfm); it is NOT a fitted uniform distribution. The swerve 3.0..3.6 m spans approximately one simulated 3.5 m lane; swDur=2.7..3.0 s ensures peak lateral acceleration pi^2*3.6/(2*2.7^2)=2.44 m/s^2 < studio.BIKE_LAT_MAX=3. Trigger 10..18 m at ego v0=12.5 m/s tests short longitudinal closing distances, chosen as a stress-test range, not a measured human gap distribution. A preliminary 18-scenario bicycle grid found avoidable contacts and informed this envelope; final evaluation uses all 1500 draws with the official seed. To infer real per-trip risk, collect bicycle-encounter frequency and trajectory/gap data on the deployment route first.
